items.followUp: Define stress and strain, and write the formula for Young’s modulus in terms of force, area, original length and extension.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of Young’s modulus and the condition under which it applies.
rubric.description: States that Young’s modulus is the ratio of stress to strain within the elastic limit.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the stress-to-strain ratio and specifying the elastic limit.

rubric.description: Writes Young’s modulus as stress divided by strain, or in an equivalent form using force and dimensions.
rubric.how: Award for either the ratio formula or the equivalent formula Y = FL/(AΔL).

modelAnswer: Young’s modulus is the ratio of stress to strain in a material, provided it is within its elastic limit.

items.followUp: State the first condition of equilibrium and write its mathematical expression.

rubric.why: Checks the meaning of rotational equilibrium.
rubric.description: States that the net torque on a body in rotational equilibrium is zero, or that clockwise and anticlockwise torques are equal.

rubric.why: Checks the mathematical expression of the second condition of equilibrium.
rubric.description: Writes the expression for rotational equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award for Στ = 0 or an expression showing the clockwise and anticlockwise torques are equal.

modelAnswer: The second condition of equilibrium states that the sum of the torques acting on a body about any point is zero.
Στ = 0, or total clockwise torque = total anticlockwise torque.
